svg.title: Emre Kalem arm - fiducial marker placement diagram (A3 landscape)
svg.text: EMRE KALEM 6-AXIS ARM - FIDUCIAL MARKER PLACEMENT
ArUco DICT_4X4_50 - 13 markers - generated by Software/arm-vision/make_placement_diagram.py from Software/vision/markers.csv and the STLs in Backups/STL_parts/
NOT AN ASSEMBLY DRAWING - see NOTES
panels + footprints + 11 of 13 sticker positions to scale; joint offsets are NOT
bbox on the arm; only a 24.8 mm
part runs out to x=+/-27.5, so
and the largest square on the
face; the part runs to x=+20. Same
Every dashed violet link is a joint whose offset is UNKNOWN - no assembly file exists here. Do not scale those gaps; the pose is for legibility only.

Violet balloon + dashed footprint: 2, 3 are NOT SURVEYED (schematic). 10 is surveyed in its OWN part's frame - which way round it mates with the part drawn is not established, so it may belong at the opposite end.
Each panel is its PART'S OWN coordinate rectangle: origin at the part bbox minimum, +u toward increasing part coordinate.
It is NOT a view from a defined direction, so which physical end is u=0 is NOT readable here - use the SURVEY CENTRE column in the schedule.
J0 base yaw - 81 deg of travel (29-110)
CURVED SURFACE - centroid and azimuth only, NOT single-tag pose.
Alt_Govde has no flat outward face: the top is open and the z=0 face is a
recessed ledge. A 20 mm sticker wrapped on r=60 spans ~19 deg of arc, ~0.8
mm of bow. The pair is 90 deg apart for COVERAGE, not for a baseline -
across 81 deg of yaw a single wrapped marker rotates out of view; this way
one of the two always faces CAM-A.
grade belongs to the marker AND its camera
joint - OFFSET UNKNOWN, not to scale
DO NOT PLACE a marker here
the FACE is surveyed; where the X is struck is not
Marker footprints are drawn at the SAME
scale as the links. The 36 mm BASE sticker
beside the 6 mm FINGER sticker is the
One 1280x720 camera at the ~550 mm standoff
needed to frame the whole arm resolves only
BASE-1/2 at pose grade and TURRET-1/2 at detect
grade. SHOULDER, ELBOW, WRIST, HAND and FINGER
are BELOW the detection floor there - not
(a) a second close camera, CAM-B at ~240 mm. One
webcam and one config entry; nothing mechanical
changes. The gripper stays marginal at 6 mm.
(b) 40 x 40 x 2 mm printed flat tabs on Alt_Kol,
On_Kol and Bilek - carries a 28 mm square,
pose-grade for the whole chain from CAM-A alone.
A 30 mm tab is NOT enough (29.6 px - detect
only). New geometry, so a proposal.
positions from Software/vision/stl-face-survey.csv; sizes from markers.csv
top edge -> the finger end of the plate
SURVEY CENTRE is where the sticker goes: sq1 = square1_cx/cy/cz_mm, sq2 = square2_cx/cy/cz_mm on the stl-face-survey.csv row for that part and face normal.
Part-frame millimetres - unambiguous without a view direction. The drawn spot is computed from it (u from the part bbox minimum, v from the bbox centre).
NOT SURVEYED = TURRET-1/2 only: Alt_Govde has no planar patch (markers.csv patch_normal cylindrical; square and baseline n/a). All others are derived.
BLACK is the ArUco square edge - the value you pass to solvePnP. STICKER is the white square you cut out (BLACK x 8/6, one module of quiet zone).
GRADE assumes f_px ~= 1108 (HFOV 60 deg at 1280 px) - UNVERIFIED. Every grade moves if that changes; run a ChArUco board to settle it.
PAIR BASELINE is only real within ONE part. Cross-part spacings have no assembly file behind them and must be observed in calibration Pass 1.
ORIENTATION is condensed from preferred_orientation in markers.csv (full text there). It defines which way is UP - it is what the arrow on every sheet-1 sticker label means.
Apply each sticker that way up EVERY time. A re-applied sticker at a different rotation silently flips the sign of that joint's residual.
- Joint-to-joint transforms. The 21 STLs are individual
parts in PRINT orientation; there is no assembly file,
URDF or STEP anywhere in the repo, so no joint axis can
- Which link belongs to which joint is INFERRED from the
Turkish part names and the measured sizes.
- D3 is DISPUTED: calibration-log.csv 2026-08-01 says the
servo on D3 was the GRIPPER, not the Base. This rig
settles it - command J0 alone and watch which link
- Until the two calibration passes run (MARKER-SYSTEM.md
6: axis identification, then datum capture at commanded
home) a marker yields a CHANGE in orientation, NOT a
- VOCABULARY: a value a camera actually saw is OBSERVED.
Nothing here observes a servo output shaft - it observes
the printed part the shaft is bolted to.
They rotate relative to their own link and must mesh.
- Mil_1/2/3 - SHAFTS. 6.8-17 mm cylinders; nothing flat,
- Jack_Cover - removable. A marker on a removable part is
- Tabla_Alt - 113.7 mm across but a RING at fill 0.22;
- Alt_Kapak - a cover; not verified rigid with any link.
- Any face flagged with an X in VIEW A.
